takeaway: A hot, sticky Friday with a dry morning and a chance of isolated afternoon storms. Nicoya could reach about 36°C. A tropical wave now arrives Saturday night, a day later than expected, so the weekend gets a bit wetter. The Caribbean trade winds, which blow offshore at Nosara, still build Sunday and peak Monday, though the marine forecast now calls them a touch lighter. A long-period south-southwest swell keeps running, with a bigger pulse around Monday. No storm threatens Costa Rica. Multi-day soaking rain stays watch-only, with Oct 16–20 the stretch to keep an eye on.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Fri–Sun, Oct 9–11)
periods.pattern: Sea breezes and daytime heat run things today. Costa Rica's weather service expects a partly cloudy morning on the North Pacific, isolated afternoon storms, and a cloudier night with possible coastal showers. Rain on the Nicoya Peninsula should stay hit-or-miss. Nicoya tops out near 36°C, hotter than yesterday. A tropical wave reaches the country Saturday night and brings more moisture, so Saturday evening and Sunday morning carry the best chance of a soaking shower. Model averages show light rain on the peninsula, with the heavier totals in the mountains and offshore.
periods.implications: Mornings are the best time for outdoor plans, especially today, when the heat is the main issue. Expect a stormy afternoon or evening somewhere nearby, and plan for a wetter Saturday night.
periods.confidence: High on the dry-morning, stormy-afternoon rhythm and the heat. Moderate on when the wave's showers actually reach Nosara.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Mon–Thu, Oct 12–15)
periods.pattern: The trades blow across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica, and all the models make Monday the strongest day. They ease Tuesday into Wednesday. Costa Rica's weather service expects moderate trades early next week. Meanwhile a low is forecast to form south of Guatemala early next week. The U.S. hurricane center now gives it a 60% chance of becoming a tropical depression within a week, moving away to the west-northwest. The European models go light and variable over Costa Rica by Wednesday and Thursday, and the latest U.S. main run shows a weak low drifting near southern Costa Rica midweek.
periods.implications: Monday should be the cleanest, least stormy day on our side. From Tuesday on, the chance of afternoon storms creeps back as the trades fade.
periods.confidence: High on Monday's trades. Moderate on Tuesday. Low to moderate on Wednesday and Thursday.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Fri–Fri, Oct 16–23)
periods.pattern: The models still split. The European AI ensemble keeps easterly winds over Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica through about Oct 21, with heavier rain on the Caribbean side and a drier Pacific side. The standard European ensemble is similar but turns a bit wetter just off our coast around Oct 18. The U.S. ensemble is wetter on the Pacific side Oct 16–22 and places a weak low south of El Salvador and Guatemala around Oct 19. The latest U.S. main run again brings a weak low close to the Nicoya coast around Oct 17, but it's on its own. Costa Rica's long-range outlook still calls for less rain than normal Oct 12–25 and very dry weather on the North Pacific from about Oct 26.
periods.implications: Still leans drier than a normal October, but keep Oct 16–20 flexible for anything rain-sensitive until the models agree.
periods.confidence: Low to moderate. The European and U.S. models disagree on how close the low gets.

surfWinds.regime: Light and variable, mostly north to northwest, through Saturday. Caribbean trades (offshore at Nosara) fill in Saturday night through Monday, peaking Monday. The marine forecast turns the wind southeast to south Monday night.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued 1:13 a.m. PDT Friday) has northeast to east wind 10–15 knots in the Gulf of Papagayo today, but north around 10 knots elsewhere, going variable under 5 knots, then northwest 10 knots tonight. Its day labels look scrambled this morning, so treat the timing below as approximate, give or take a day. It shows north 10 knots, then north to northeast 10 knots, then northeast 10 knots into the weekend. Sunday is northeast to east around 10 knots, Sunday night east to southeast 10 knots, and Monday east 10–15 knots. That's the real Caribbean trade, offshore for Nosara. Monday night swings southeast to south 10 knots, which is cross-shore to side-onshore. That's a little lighter than yesterday's 10–15 knots for Sunday. North wind is close to cross-shore here and northwest is side-onshore. Light and variable doesn't mean glassy offshore; it just means no trade wind, so the sea breeze takes over by late morning. Seas run 3–5 feet with long 15–17 second periods through the weekend, rising to 4–6 feet from the south-southwest, then 5–7 feet around Monday at 15–16 seconds. Nicaragua: every model shows the trades blowing across Nicaragua and out over the Pacific Sunday into Tuesday, and the European ensembles keep them over Nicaragua to about Oct 21. All-day offshore in Nicaragua would point to strong, clean Nosara mornings, but it doesn't mean all-day offshore here.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Today and Saturday, dawn patrol before the sea breeze. The long-period swell is worth the early start. Sunday morning through Monday morning (Oct 11–12) is the best offshore window, with Monday the strongest trade day and the bigger swell. Tuesday morning could still be clean if the trades hang on, but plan on a shorter window.
surfWinds.confidence: High on light winds through Saturday and trades Sunday into Monday. Moderate on how strong they get at the coast. Low to moderate from Tuesday on.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only, nothing established. About the same as yesterday, with a slight uptick in the hurricane center's odds.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Oct 16–20, mostly from the U.S. models, with the wettest area mainly just offshore.
gyreWatch.supporting: The hurricane center raised the chance of a tropical depression south of Guatemala to 60% within a week (up from 50%). The U.S. ensemble spreads heavier rain over the Pacific waters off Central America Oct 16–22 and places a weak low south of El Salvador and Guatemala around Oct 19. The U.S. main run again brings a weak low near the Nicoya coast around Oct 17, the kind of setup that draws in Pacific moisture for several days. The standard European ensemble turns a bit wetter just off our coast around Oct 18. The marine forecast's southerly turn Monday night fits a low beginning to pull Pacific air in.
gyreWatch.conflicting: The European AI ensemble keeps easterly trades over Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica through about Oct 21 and puts the heavier rain on the Caribbean side, which usually means a drier Pacific coast. The hurricane center expects the low to move away to the west-northwest. The U.S. main run's close-in low isn't supported by the ensemble averages. Costa Rica's long-range outlook calls for less rain than normal Oct 12–25. The U.S. tropics outlook, last updated Oct 6, expects below-normal Caribbean rain and doesn't flag a Central American gyre.

whatChanged: The tropical wave now arrives Saturday night instead of Friday, per Costa Rica's new weekly outlook, which also calls for moderate trades early next week. The marine forecast trims Sunday's trade to about 10 knots (from 10–15) and makes Monday the strongest day. The bigger swell pulse now looks like Monday rather than Monday night. The hurricane center raised the low south of Guatemala to 60% (from 50%). Today's Nicoya high is hotter, about 36°C against 32.5°C yesterday. Costa Rica's weather service issued an afternoon storm alert Thursday morning. The long-range outlooks are unchanged.
practical: Get outside early today and stay hydrated in the heat. Expect isolated afternoon storms, and a wetter Saturday night and Sunday morning as the tropical wave passes. Surf dawn patrol for the long-period swell, and circle Sunday and Monday mornings (Oct 11–12) for the cleanest offshore surf, Monday especially. Keep Oct 16–20 flexible. No tropical storm threat to Costa Rica.
